narrative.title: Re-ranking the Entire Work Queue
narrative.scenario: A job scheduler's queue is a one-way chain whose entries landed in arbitrary priority order, and the dispatcher needs the whole chain ascending without exporting it to an array — memory is reserved for the chain itself. The viable strategy is merge sort: split the chain at the middle, sort each half the same way, then zip two already-sorted chains together.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of node values representing the linked list.
narrative.outputFormat: The values of the list sorted in ascending order.

testCases.explanation: Four scrambled entries come out fully ascending after the split-sort-merge rounds.
Negatives and zero rank below the positives in the merged chain.

hintLevels: Level 1: Sorting a chain you cannot index means divide-and-conquer with relinking, not element swapping.
Level 2: Cut the chain at the middle (slow/fast), sort both halves recursively, then merge two sorted chains by always advancing the smaller head.
Level 3: The split must terminate recursion — after finding the middle, sever it (middle.next = null) or the halves never shrink; the recursive stack is the only extra memory, hence O(log n).
